explanations.explanation: I get it, friend, walking in your sins sure sounds like a solo project. But Paul says they walked that way when they "conformed to the ways of this world and of the ruler of the power of the air" (Ephesians 2:2). Conformed! Somebody else was cutting the shape. It's like a cookie bragging it's one of a kind when three hundred of its cousins came off the exact same stamp.

YES, baker, nobody was flying solo. Paul says they "conformed to the ways of this world and of the ruler of the power of the air, the spirit who is now at work in the sons of disobedience" (Ephesians 2:2). That's not one person doing their own thing. That's a whole crowd walking in step, following the same pattern.

THERE it is. Paul writes, "All of us also lived among them at one time, fulfilling the cravings of our flesh and indulging its desires and thoughts" (Ephesians 2:3). He doesn't stand outside the oven pointing at everybody else's cookies. He climbs right onto the tray with the whole batch, and honestly, friend, I love him for it.

Paul could've kept the spotlight on them, but listen to how he shifts. Verse 1 says "you were dead in your trespasses and sins," and then verse 3 says "All of us also lived among them at one time" (Ephesians 2:1, 3). He goes from "you" to "us" and drops himself right into the dough. That's the coworker who says, "Who left the oven on?" and then sighs, "Okay. It was me. It was ALL of us."

The sons of disobedience are where that spirit "is now at work" (Ephesians 2:2). But then Paul writes, "All of us also lived among them at one time" (Ephesians 2:3). Among them! Paul isn't pointing across the street at those people, friend. He's saying we had an address on that street too.

MERCY, baker! Paul says, "But because of His great love for us, God, who is rich in mercy," steps in (Ephesians 2:4). And He's not a little bit merciful, He's RICH in it. When you're by nature children of wrath (Ephesians 2:3), that's the one account balance you want to hear about.

God is wise, no doubt about it (Romans 16:27), but that's not the word Paul picks here. He writes, "God, who is rich in mercy" (Ephesians 2:4). Think about who He's stepping in for: people Paul calls "by nature children of wrath" (Ephesians 2:3). Folks in that spot don't need a smarter plan first, friend. They need mercy, and God's got it by the truckload.

I see why that one came to mind, friend, with all that talk of wrath. But Paul writes, "But because of His great love for us, God, who is rich in mercy," (Ephesians 2:4). That little word "But" is doing some HEAVY lifting. Right after "children of wrath" (Ephesians 2:3), Paul doesn't reach for justice. He reaches for great love and mercy.

Oh, I wish I could take credit for cleaning up, friend, but the verse won't let me. Paul says God "made us alive with Christ even when we were dead in our trespasses" (Ephesians 2:5). Even when we were DEAD. Dead people don't tidy up. That's like waiting for the cookie dough to roll itself out and hop in the oven.

You got it, baker. Paul says God "made us alive with Christ even when we were dead in our trespasses" (Ephesians 2:5). No cleanup first. No "get your life together and call Me back." God moved while we were still dead, and that's the whole point.

explanations.answer: With Him in the heavenly realms
explanations.explanation: Heavenly realms, friend! Paul says God "raised us up with Christ and seated us with Him in the heavenly realms in Christ Jesus" (Ephesians 2:6). Not standing in the back. Not waiting in the lobby. SEATED. Somebody who was dead in verse 1 now has a seat with Christ, and I'm still not over it.

Mount Zion is a big name in the Bible (Psalm 48:2), so I see the pull. But here Paul says God "seated us with Him in the heavenly realms in Christ Jesus" (Ephesians 2:6). He doesn't name a mountain at all. Paul's pointing higher than any hilltop, friend.

Jerusalem makes sense as a guess, baker, but Paul doesn't name a city here. He says God "raised us up with Christ and seated us with Him in the heavenly realms in Christ Jesus" (Ephesians 2:6). Notice it's "with Christ" and "with Him" every step of the way. Paul keeps the focus on who we're with, not on a spot on a map.

Ha! If the display was about how hard I worked, friend, they'd need a VERY small display case. Paul says God did it so that "in the coming ages He might display the surpassing riches of His grace" (Ephesians 2:7). The thing on show is His grace and His kindness to us in Christ Jesus. We're not the trophy, we're the proof of how kind He is.

Right, baker, nobody's work goes in the spotlight. Paul says God did it so that "in the coming ages He might display the surpassing riches of His grace, demonstrated by His kindness to us in Christ Jesus" (Ephesians 2:7). Surpassing riches! That means grace that goes past anything you could stack next to it. God is putting His grace on display, and it's going to run for ages.

GIFT! Paul says, "For it is by grace you have been saved through faith, and this not from yourselves; it is the gift of God," (Ephesians 2:8). A gift is something you receive, not something you clock in for. Nobody hands you a present and then slides you an invoice, friend.

A reward sounds nice, friend, but a reward means you did something to win it. Paul says, "and this not from yourselves; it is the gift of God," (Ephesians 2:8). Not from yourselves! You don't get a medal for being rescued from the back of the drawer, trust me. Somebody just opens the drawer.

A wage is what you get for putting in the hours, baker, and Paul shuts that door. He says, "and this not from yourselves; it is the gift of God," (Ephesians 2:8). Then he adds right away that it's "not by works" (Ephesians 2:9). There's no time card for this one. You can stop looking for the punch clock.

That's it, friend. Paul says salvation is "not by works, so that no one can boast" (Ephesians 2:9). If you didn't bake it, you can't brag about it. Imagine somebody walking around a party taking bows for a cookie box somebody else filled. NOBODY gets to do that here.

Paul doesn't say anything here about asking, baker. He says it's "not by works, so that no one can boast" (Ephesians 2:9). The thing that gets shut down is bragging. Paul calls it "the gift of God" (Ephesians 2:8), so nobody gets to strut around like they earned it.

Oh, thanking God is not what's off the table, friend! Paul says it's "not by works, so that no one can boast" (Ephesians 2:9). Boasting is what goes. If a gift leaves you with nothing to brag about, about the only thing left to say is thank you.

explanations.answer: Good works God prepared in advance
explanations.explanation: BEAUTIFUL, baker. Paul says we are "created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God prepared in advance as our way of life" (Ephesians 2:10). He prepared them in ADVANCE. Good works aren't how we get in the door. God lays them out ahead of time, like a baker who sets every cutter on the counter before the dough is even ready.

explanations.answer: Good works that earn His grace
explanations.explanation: Can't earn a gift, friend, Paul just told us that. Grace saves "through faith, and this not from yourselves; it is the gift of God, not by works" (Ephesians 2:8-9). Then he says we're "created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God prepared in advance as our way of life" (Ephesians 2:10). Good works don't come before grace to earn it. They come after, because God made us for them.

explanations.answer: Good works that pay off our sins
explanations.explanation: Paul never sends a bill, baker. He says we're "created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God prepared in advance as our way of life" (Ephesians 2:10). Back in verse 5, God made us alive while we were dead in our trespasses, and Paul says, "It is by grace you have been saved!" (Ephesians 2:5). The good works are our way of life now, not a payment plan.
